problem: Amazon wanted a device to tie customers more closely to its shopping and content.
title: Amazon launches the Fire Phone and discontinues it a year later
context: Amazon entered the smartphone market in July 2014 at a premium price.
decision_made: Launch its own smartphone, the Fire Phone.
action_taken: Cut the price sharply within two months and disclosed a $170 million charge in October 2014.
observed_outcome: Sales were weak, Amazon took a $170 million charge for inventory and supplier commitments, and the phone was discontinued in 2015.
lessons: A premium hardware entry into a mature market without a clear advantage can be costly.
limitations: Sources disagree on discontinuation timing and quote different prices because of contract versus unlocked pricing.

claims.claim_text: Amazon launched the Fire Phone in July 2014.
Amazon took a $170 million charge and later discontinued the phone.
